title: Homemade Biscuits
description: Buttery, soft biscuits made completely from scratch, with all butter and no shortening.

items.note: very cold; unsalted European butter is ideal but not required

steps: For the flakiest biscuits, chill the butter in the freezer for 10 to 20 minutes before you start. It should be very cold.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, mix the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt well.

Take the butter out of the freezer and either cut it into the flour mixture with a pastry cutter or (preferred) shred it on a box grater and stir it in. Keep working it in until the mixture looks like coarse crumbs.
Add the milk and stir with a wooden spoon or spatula just until combined. Don't overwork the dough.
Turn the dough out onto a well-floured surface and gently bring it together with your hands, adding flour if it's too sticky.
Fold the dough in half over itself and gently press the layers together. Turn it 90 degrees and fold again. Repeat 5 to 6 times, taking care not to overwork it.
With your hands (not a rolling pin), flatten the dough to 1 inch (2.5 cm) thick. Lightly flour a 2¾-inch (7 cm) round cutter.
Cut biscuits close together, pressing the cutter straight down, and set them less than ½ inch (1 cm) apart on the baking sheet. Gently re-work the scraps to cut a biscuit or two more.
Bake for 12 minutes, or until the tops are just starting to turn light golden brown.
If you like, brush with melted salted butter as soon as they come out of the oven. Serve warm.

notes: This recipe can be doubled to make 12 biscuits.
Whole milk is the default, but buttermilk and 2% milk both work.
